chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja'far ibn Bashir from al-Hasan al-Sayqal said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'The child belongs to the one who has the concubine, and let him be patient for the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): The child belongs to the bed (of the master), and for the fornicator is the stone.'
ai.seo_question: Who does the child of a concubine belong to according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* reinforces the foundational juristic principle of *al-waladu lil-firashi* (the child follows the bed/master) specifically within the context of *kitabah* or ownership of a concubine, ensuring lineage legitimacy. It highlights the master's obligation to maintain patience and stability regarding the child's status, distinguishing the legitimate offspring from the *zani* (fornicator) whose lineage is not attached to the child. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh in determining inheritance and marital prohibitions arising from consanguinity through concubinage.
